title: One Prayer I Have, — All Prayers in One
description: One Prayer I Have, — All Prayers in One in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 521, “Prayer for Submission”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: One prayer I have, all prayers in one, When I am whol-ly Thine; Thy will, my God, Thy will be done, And let that will be mine.

lines: One prayer I have, — all prayers in one,
Thy will, my God, Thy will be done,
And let that will be mine.
May I remember that to Thee
And back in gratitude from me
Thy gifts are only then enjoyed,
And though Thy wisdom takes away,
No, let me bless Thy name, and say
A pilgrim through the earth I roam,
And all must fail when I go home,
For this is not my rest.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
